title: The influence of the ionic component of the electrical conductivity on the semiconductor-metal transition in liquid Tl-Se alloys

segments.text: Experimental investigations of electrical conductivity sigma (T) and thermo-e.m.f.
S(T) were performed for liquid TI-Se alloys in the region of the stoichiometric compound Tl,Se in a wide temperature range (from 600 K to 1700 K).
It was shown that the existence of an ionic component in the electrical conductivity affects significantly the peculiarities of the metallization process of the liquid cells.

A model explaining the unusual thermo-e.m.f. behavior, which forms a large deviation from the 'classical' dependence in a wide temperature range resulted from the effect of electron-hole compensation, has been proposed.
The ionic contribution essentially changes the electrical conductivity resulting in a deformation of the exponential curve sigma (T).

segments.text: The temperature dependent thermoelectric power and resistivity for a series of disordered (Nd0.8-xPr0.2Cax)Ba2Cu3O7-delta with 0 less than or equal to x less than or equal to 0.20 has been measured in order to study the disorder effect induced by Pr-doping, in which 50% of the Pr ion is in the Pr(IV) state deduced from unit cell volumes.
The hole concentration in CuO2 planes (P-sh) of the samples has been estimated from the oxygen stoichiometry.
T-c-suppression by Pr-doping could not be recovered by increasing p(sh), demonstrating that the ionic disorder effect plays an important role on Pr-doped samples.

title: Multifunctional Pb-free double perovskites M2MoRuO6 (M = Ba, Sr) with narrow band gaps for advanced electronic and optoelectronic applications: Insights from first-principles calculations

segments.text: This study employs first-principles density functional theory to comprehensively examine the structural, electronic, optical, mechanical, thermoelectric, and thermophysical properties of Pb-free double perovskites M2MoRuO6 (M = Ba, Sr), aiming to assess their potential for multifunctional applications.

The optimized structures exhibit mechanical and dynamical stability in accordance with the Born stability criteria, and the obtained tolerance and octahedral factors fall within the stability range expected for double perovskite compounds.

Electronic structure calculations using the TB-mBJ potential reveal narrow indirect band gaps (0.38 eV for Ba2MoRuO6 and 0.32 eV for Sr2MoRuO6), low effective masses, and p-type semiconducting behavior, suggesting high carrier mobility, which are suitable for optoelectronic devices.
Optical studies demonstrate strong absorption in the infrared and visible ranges (0.47-3.26 eV), while redox potential calculations suggest promising photocatalytic activity.

The phonon dispersion spectra and elastic constants validate dynamic and mechanical stability, respectively, with mixed ionic-covalent bonding confirmed through charge density and Mulliken population analyses.

Thermoelectric evaluation yields high Seebeck coefficients (>= 200 & micro;V K-1), significant power factors, and remarkable thermoelectric performance, with ZT values exceeding 1.6 at room temperature and approaching 2.4 at elevated temperatures when lattice thermal conductivity is taken into account, confirming the strong potential of these materials for energy-conversion applications.

Thermophysical properties, including high Debye (430.72 K for Ba2MoRuO6 and 440.82 K for Sr2MoRuO6) and melting temperatures and Gr & uuml;neisen parameter, indicate strong bonding, excellent thermal stability, and suitability for high-temperature applications.

Thus, M2MoRuO6 (M = Ba, Sr) emerges as a multifunctional class of double perovskites with potential applications in next-generation electronic, optoelectronic, photocatalytic, and thermoelectric devices.

title: Thermoelectric properties of Gd/W double substituted calcium manganite

segments.text: Nearly dense polycrystalline samples of Ca1-xGdxMn1-xWxO3-delta with Gd/W double substitution (0 <= x <= 0.03) were prepared by the mixed-oxide route and their thermoelectric properties were evaluated in the temperature range 25 degrees C-700 degrees C.
All samples are single-phase with an orthorhombic perovsldte structure.
At higher temperatures the samples are nonstoichiometric, and a phase transition from orthorhombic to cubic occurs with the transition temperature systematically increasing with x.

Double substitution with Gd and W leads to increased electrical conductivity and reduced thermopower, resulting in a maximum of the power factor of 370 mu W/(K(2)m) for the composition x = 0.01 at 300 degrees C.
Charge transport in the samples is discussed as polaron hopping type transport.
The values of the Seebeck coefficient are interpreted with Helices formula and imply a small nonstoichiometry of the samples.
The thermal conductivity is decreased with increasing x, and for x = 0.03 a K = 3.2 W/mK is observed at 100 degrees C.
Double substituted calcium manganite with x = 0.01 exhibits a figure of merit ZT = 0.12 at 700 degrees C.

title: Optical and structural properties of PbSe films obtained by ionic exchange of lead oxyhydroxicarbonate in a selenium-rongalite solution

segments.text: In this work, starting from precursor films of Pla(10)O(OH)(6)(CO3)(6), previously obtained by chemical bath deposition technique, we report the process to obtain PbSe films through ionic exchange.
For this, after chemical deposition, several pieces of the precursor films were immersed in selenium ions solution in order to promote the transformation to PbSe films by ionic exchange.
Instead using the conventional sodium selenium sulfite solution as the selenium ions solution, a new one is reported, which is based in rongalite (CH3NaO3S) and sodium citrate as reducing agents.
Samples were removed after 30, 60 and 90 min to determine the effects of ionic exchange time on the phase transformation process.
The complete set of samples was analyzed by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy and optical absorption measurements.
The XRD results show a gradual crystalline transformation from the precursor phase to cubic PbSe crystalline phase.
The gradual phase transformation is accompanied by surface morphologic changes as shown by SEM images.
From the optical absorption spectrum of the PbSe films, it was calculated the energy band gap, being around 0.34 eV.

segments.text: The thermopower (S) of Ce1-xLaxCu4Al (0.0 <= x <= 1.0) compounds is presented.
Over the studied temperature range, it is found that the thermopower is positive and shows a maximum except for pure LaCu4Al.
A large positive peak in S(T) dependence is attributed to an interplay between a Kondo scattering and the crystal field.
The maximum of thermopower shifts slightly from 27 K to 25 K upon La concentration.
Due to the larger ionic radius of the La compared to the Ce ion the lattice is expanded for increasing x.
Such expansion weakens the hybridization of the f moments with the conduction electrons and thus lowers the Kondo temperature.
Based on band model the position and width of the 4f peak nearest to the Fermi level have been estimated.

title: First-principles calculations of structural and bonding properties of Li-doped tetrahedrite thermoelectrics

segments.text: Tetrahedrite (copper antimony sulfosalt) is a promising p-type thermoelectric material due to its very low intrinsic thermal conductivity and moderately-high power factor, with one of the limitations being the lack of n-type variant to create a thermoelectric generator.
In this paper, DFT calculations have been carried out to study tetrahedrite doped with Li into structural voids, LixCu(12)Sb(4)S(13) (0 <= x <= 3).
Enthalpies of formation show that the introduction of Li into both 6b and 24 g sites is energetically favorable.
Dopants in those positions differently affect the rattling Cu(12e) behavior, as well as vary in the magnitude of induced local disorder.
Topological analysis of charge density classifies tetrahedrite as a closed-shell, ionic system of interactions with some degree of covalency.
The addition of Li increases bond strain and decreases structural stability.

Electronic band structure shows that for x > 2.0, material becomes n-type; however, results are not precisely conclusive on whether structure will be synthesizable, which should be determined experimentally.

These properties, including low thermal conductivity and thermal expansion, make both compounds promising for thermoelectric applications.
Additional analysis of optical properties indicates strong light absorption in the visible range.
